title: Tracing the Latent Threads: A Mechanistic Study of How LLMs Represent and Operationalize Race and Ethnicity Cues
abstract: arXiv:2601.12868v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly operate in high-stakes settings where demographic attributes such as race and ethnicity may be explicitly stated or implicitly suggested through textual cues. However, existing studies primarily document outcome-level disparities, offering limited insight into internal mechanisms underlying these effects. We present a mechanistic study of how race and ethnicity cues are represented and operationalized within LLMs. Using two publicly available datasets spanning toxicity-related generation and clinical narrative understanding tasks, we analyze three open-source models with a reproducible interpretability pipeline combining probing, neuron-level attribution, and targeted intervention. We find that sensitivity to demographic cues is distributed across internal units and varies substantially across models. translated_title: 追溯潜在线索：大语言模型如何表征与运用种族和民族线索的机制研究
translated_abstract: arXiv:2601.12868v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地运行于高风险场景中，在这些场景里，种族和民族等人口统计属性可能被明确表述，也可能通过文本线索被隐含暗示。然而，现有研究主要记录结果层面的差异，对这些效应背后的内部机制提供的洞察有限。我们对种族和民族线索在大语言模型内部如何被表征和运用开展了一项机制研究。利用两个公开可用的数据集（涵盖毒性相关生成任务和临床叙事理解任务），我们通过结合探测、神经元级归因和针对性干预的可复现可解释性流水线，分析了三个开源模型。我们发现，对人口统计线索的敏感性分布于模型的多个内部单元之中，且在不同模型之间存在显著差异。这些单元往往与相互纠缠的语义面向保持一致，包括明确的群体标签、地理……
tldr: 该论文通过探测、神经元级归因和针对性干预等可解释性方法，机制性地揭示了种族和民族线索在大语言模型内部的表征与运用方式，发现对人口统计线索的敏感性广泛分布于多个内部单元且在不同模型间差异显著。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a mechanistic study of how race and ethnicity cues are represented and operationalized within LLMs, using probing, neuron-level attribution, and targeted interventions to show that sensitivity to demographic cues is distributed across internal units and varies substantially across models.
